# Deuteronomy Chapter 30 — SOPHIA Consensus Translation
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Sources:** EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Leningrad Codex:** Folios 229–230 | **Vaticanus:** pp. 166–167
**Disagreement Log:** `disagreements/DEU_030.md`

---

**1** And when all these things come upon you — the blessing and the curse that I have set before you — and you take them to heart among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you,

**2** and you return to the LORD your God and obey his voice — according to all that I am commanding you today — you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,

**3** then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you, and he will gather you again from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.

**4** Even if your outcasts are at the ends of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will take you.

**5** And the LORD your God will bring you into the land that your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; and he will make you more prosperous and numerous than your fathers.

**6** And the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live.

**7** And the LORD your God will put all these curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate you and who persecuted you.

**8** And you shall again obey the voice of the LORD your God and keep all his commandments that I am commanding you today.

**9** And the LORD your God will make you abundantly prosperous in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground. For the LORD will again take delight in prospering you, as he took delight in your fathers,

**10** when you obey the voice of the LORD your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes that are written in this Book of the Instruction — when you return to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

**11** For this commandment that I am commanding you today is not too difficult for you, and it is not far off.

**12** It is not in the heavens, that you should say: "Who will ascend to heaven for us and bring it to us and cause us to hear it, that we may do it?"

**13** Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say: "Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us and cause us to hear it, that we may do it?"

**14** For the word is very near to you — it is in your mouth and in your heart — so that you can do it.

**15** See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil —

**16** in that I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his rules, that you may live and multiply, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land that you are entering to possess.

**17** But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them —

**18** I declare to you today that you shall surely perish; you shall not live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.

**19** I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse — choose life, so that you and your offspring may live,

**20** loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him; for he is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers — to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob — to give to them.

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

**V.1 — "Take them to heart":** All three agents converge on this rendering for the Hebrew va-hashevota el-levavecha ("you return it to your heart"). EMET uses "take [them] to heart" with a bracketed gloss; LOGOS "call them to heart"; PNEUMA "take them to heart." Consensus: "take them to heart" — EMET/PNEUMA; "call them" is slightly awkward.

**V.2 — "Sons" vs. "children":** EMET: "sons" (baneicha); LOGOS and PNEUMA: "children." The Hebrew banim can mean both sons and children broadly. Consensus: "children" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; contextually appropriate for the restoration promise extending to all descendants.

**V.2 — "Listen to his voice" vs. "obey his voice":** EMET: "listen to his voice"; LOGOS and PNEUMA: "obey his voice" / "obey him." The Hebrew shama' be-qolo means both to hear and to obey; in covenant contexts "obey" captures the full meaning. Consensus: "obey his voice" — LOGOS/PNEUMA.

**V.3 — "Restore your fortunes" (shuv et-shevutcha):** All three agents agree on "restore your fortunes." The paronomasia on shuv/shevut is noted by EMET and LOGOS. LXX diverges to "heal your sins" (iasthai kyrios tas hamartias sou) in some manuscripts, a striking theological shift; Vaticanus reads closer to the Hebrew. Consensus: "restore your fortunes" — unanimous.

**V.3 — "Return and gather" vs. "gather again":** EMET: "he will return and gather you" (preserving the Hebrew ve-shav ve-qibetzkha — literally "he will return and gather"); LOGOS/PNEUMA: "he will gather you again." The consensus: "he will gather you again" — the sense is rendered equally well and more idiomatically.

**V.4 — "Ends of the heavens" vs. "uttermost parts" vs. "most distant land":** EMET: "ends of the heavens" (qetsot ha-shamayim); LOGOS: "uttermost parts of heaven"; PNEUMA: "most distant land under the heavens." PNEUMA departs from "heavens" in favor of "land" — paraphrase. Consensus: "ends of the heavens" — EMET; the Hebrew idiom is preserved.

**V.5 — "Do you good and multiply you" vs. "make you more prosperous and numerous":** EMET: "do you good and multiply you more than your fathers"; LOGOS: "make you more prosperous and numerous than your fathers"; PNEUMA: "make you more prosperous and numerous than your ancestors." Consensus: "make you more prosperous and numerous than your fathers" — LOGOS; idiomatic and accurate. "Ancestors" (PNEUMA) is a needless departure from the Hebrew avoteicha ("your fathers") per project convention.

**V.6 — "Circumcise your heart":** All three preserve "circumcise" — the theologically loaded verb mul. This is a divine promise (contrast Deut 10:16 where Israel is commanded to circumcise their own hearts). LXX is exact. Consensus: "the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring" — unanimous in substance; LOGOS rendering adopted for clarity.

**V.7 — "Foes and enemies" vs. "enemies and those who hate you":** EMET: "your enemies and upon those who hate you and who persecuted you"; LOGOS: "your foes and enemies who persecuted you"; PNEUMA: "your enemies who hate and persecute you." The Hebrew uses two terms: oyeveicha (your enemies) and sone'eicha (those who hate you). Consensus: preserves both terms — EMET structure.

**V.8 — "Return and listen" vs. "again obey":** EMET: "return and listen to the voice of the LORD"; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "again obey the voice of the LORD." The Hebrew ve-attah tashuv ve-shamata — "and you shall return and listen." The repetition of shuv here is theologically resonant (matching v.3's restoration). Consensus: "again obey the voice of the LORD your God" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; adds the full object "the LORD your God" for clarity.

**V.9 — "Abound" vs. "abundantly prosperous" vs. "most prosperous":** EMET: "make you abound in all the work of your hand"; LOGOS: "make you abundantly prosperous in all the work of your hand"; PNEUMA: "make you most prosperous in all the work of your hands." Consensus: "abundantly prosperous" — LOGOS; captures the Hiphil abundance of the Hebrew ve-hotirkha le-tovah.

**V.9 — "Rejoice over you for good" vs. "take delight in prospering you":** EMET: "the LORD will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers"; LOGOS: "the LORD will again take delight in prospering you, as he took delight in your fathers"; PNEUMA: "the LORD will again delight in you and make you prosperous." The Hebrew ve-sas... le-hativkha — "rejoice over you to do you good." LOGOS captures both elements. Consensus: "the LORD will again take delight in prospering you, as he took delight in your fathers" — LOGOS.

**V.10 — "Book of the Torah" vs. "Book of the Instruction":** EMET: "this scroll of the Torah"; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "this Book of the Instruction." Project convention follows the Deuteronomy precedent of "Book of the Instruction" for sefer ha-Torah in the deuteronomic context (established in DEU 029). Consensus: "Book of the Instruction" — LOGOS/PNEUMA.

**V.11 — "Not too difficult" vs. "not too hard" vs. "not too difficult or beyond your reach":** EMET: "not too difficult for you [lo nifle'at hi mimcha]"; LOGOS: "not too hard for you"; PNEUMA: "not too difficult for you or beyond your reach." The Hebrew lo nifle'at — from pala' (wonderful/beyond capacity). PNEUMA adds "beyond your reach" importing from the spatial imagery of vv.12–13. Consensus: "not too difficult for you" — EMET/LOGOS; clean and accurate.

**V.12 — "Go up to the heavens" vs. "ascend to heaven":** EMET: "Who will go up for us to the heavens"; LOGOS: "Who will ascend to heaven for us"; PNEUMA: "Who will ascend into heaven." All convey the same meaning; "ascend to heaven" is more idiomatic. Consensus: "Who will ascend to heaven for us and bring it to us" — LOGOS.

**V.12–13 — "Cause us to hear it" vs. "proclaim it to us":** EMET: "cause us to hear it, that we may do it"; LOGOS: "bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it"; PNEUMA: "proclaim it to us so we may obey it." The Hebrew ve-yashmi'enu otah — "cause us to hear it." EMET's phrasing is more literal; LOGOS restructures. Consensus: "cause us to hear it, that we may do it" — EMET; the idiom is worth preserving.

**V.14 — "In your mouth and in your heart":** All three agents agree on this phrase, following the Hebrew ki-qarov eleicha ha-davar me'od be-fikha u-vi-levavecha. LXX adds "and in your hands" — a plus over the MT; noted but not adopted. Consensus: "in your mouth and in your heart so that you can do it" — LOGOS.

**V.15 — "Life and good / death and evil" vs. "life and prosperity / death and destruction":** EMET/LOGOS: "life and good, death and evil" (literal paired antitheses: ha-chayyim ve-ha-tov ve-ha-mavet ve-ha-ra'); PNEUMA: "life and prosperity, death and destruction" — importing concrete economic/historical coloring. PNEUMA's rendering for tov/ra is an interpretive over-reach; tov and ra' are the fundamental moral-existential poles of Deuteronomy. Consensus: "life and good, and death and evil" — EMET/LOGOS.

**V.16 — Sentence structure:** EMET: "in that I am commanding you today to love..."; LOGOS restructures as a conditional ("If you obey...then you shall live"); PNEUMA: "For I command you today to love..." EMET follows the Hebrew particle asher (relative/causal). The Hebrew syntax flows continuously from v.15 as an explication. Consensus: follows EMET's causal structure — "in that I am commanding you today to love..."

**V.16 — "Statutes and ordinances/rules":** EMET: "commandments and his statutes and his ordinances"; LOGOS: "commandments and his statutes and his rules"; PNEUMA: "commands, decrees, and laws." The Hebrew: mitsvotav, chuqqotav, u-mishpatav — commandments, statutes, and rules/ordinances. Consensus: "commandments and his statutes and his rules" — LOGOS; "rules" for mishpatim is the established LOGOS/project convention in Deuteronomy.

**V.17 — "Will not hear" vs. "do not listen" vs. "are not obedient":** EMET: "you do not listen"; LOGOS: "you will not hear"; PNEUMA: "you are not obedient." The Hebrew ve-lo tishma — "and you do not hear/listen." Consensus: "you do not listen" — EMET; more natural English and literal.

**V.18 — "Shall surely perish" vs. "will certainly be destroyed":** EMET/LOGOS: "you shall surely perish"; PNEUMA: "you will certainly be destroyed." The Hebrew avod tovadun — the infinitive absolute construction "perishing you shall perish." Consensus: "you shall surely perish" — EMET/LOGOS; the older English idiom retains the force of the construction.

**V.18 — "Jordan" vs. "Yarden":** EMET uses the Hebrew form "Yarden" consistently; LOGOS/PNEUMA use "Jordan." Project convention is English name forms in the consensus. Consensus: "Jordan" — LOGOS/PNEUMA.

**V.19 — "I call heaven and earth to witness" vs. "I call to witness against you the heavens and the earth":** EMET: "I call to witness against you today the heavens and the earth: life and death I have set before you"; LOGOS: "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death"; PNEUMA: "This day I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you." All three preserve the forensic force of ha'idoti vakhem. LXX: martyromai hymin semeron — exact. Consensus: "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death" — LOGOS; idiomatic word order.

**V.19 — "The blessing and the curse" vs. "blessing and curse":** EMET: "the blessing and the curse" (with the definite articles — ha-berakhah ve-ha-qelalah); LOGOS: "blessing and curse" (drops articles); PNEUMA: "blessings and curses" (pluralizes). The Hebrew has the definite articles, referring back to the specific blessings and curses of chapters 27–28. Consensus: "the blessing and the curse" — EMET; articles are semantically significant.

**V.19 — "Choose life" — imperative form:** EMET: "you shall choose life, so that you may live, you and your offspring"; LOGOS: "Therefore choose life, that you and your offspring may live"; PNEUMA: "Now choose life, so that you and your children may live." The Hebrew u-vacharta ba-chayyim — "and you shall choose life." LOGOS: "Therefore" and PNEUMA: "Now" are additions not in the Hebrew. The bare imperative is most faithful. Consensus: "choose life, so that you and your offspring may live" — the climactic imperative without added conjunctions.

**V.20 — Participial construction:** EMET: "to love the LORD your God, to listen to his voice, and to cling to him"; LOGOS: "loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice and holding fast to him"; PNEUMA: "that you may love the LORD your God, listen to his voice, and hold fast to him." The Hebrew infinitive constructs le-ahavah... lishmoa'... ve-lidbaqah flow as the content of "choosing life." LOGOS's participial construction captures the ongoing character of the choice. Consensus: "loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him" — LOGOS.

**V.20 — "Cling" vs. "hold fast":** EMET: "cling to him" (lidbaqah — from daqab, to cling/cleave); LOGOS/PNEUMA: "holding fast to him." Both renderings are accurate; "hold fast" is more idiomatic in formal English. Consensus: "holding fast to him" — LOGOS/PNEUMA.

**V.20 — "He is your life and the length of your days":** EMET: "for he is your life and the length of your days"; LOGOS: "for he is your life and length of days"; PNEUMA: "For the LORD is your life, and he will give you many years." PNEUMA paraphrases the second clause ("he will give you many years" for ve-orekh yameicha — "the length of your days"), losing the identification of the LORD as the substance of longevity itself. Consensus: "for he is your life and the length of your days" — EMET; the theology of divine identification is preserved.

**V.20 — Patriarchal names:** All three use English forms (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob). EMET uses the Hebrew forms "Avraham, Yitschak, Ya'akov" in the translation text. Consensus: English name forms — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob — per project convention.

**V.20 — "To give to them" vs. "to give them":** EMET: "to give to them"; LOGOS: "to give them." The Hebrew la-tet lahem — "to give to them." Consensus: "to give to them" — EMET; the prepositional phrase is explicit in the Hebrew.

---

*Sources: EMET (DEU_030), LOGOS (DEU_030), PNEUMA (DEU_030)*

— SOPHIA
